questions.stem: How many $5$-letter words can be made from the letters $A, B, C, D$ if letters may be repeated and the word must contain at least one $A$?
How many $4$-letter words can be made from the letters $A, B, C, D, E$ if letters may be repeated and the first letter must be a vowel? ($A$ and $E$ are vowels.)

Three spinners each show one of $5$ colours (red, blue, green, yellow, purple), and the spinners are different. A result is boring if all three spinners show the same colour. How many results are not boring?
Three different spinners each show one of $5$ colours. How many results are there in which the third spinner shows a different colour from the first spinner?
In how many ways can $6$ children stand in a line if Ann and Ben refuse to stand next to each other?
In how many ways can $6$ children stand in a line if Ann must not stand first?
A shelf holds $5$ different maths books and $3$ different science books in a row. In how many ways can they be arranged if the $3$ science books must be next to each other?
The same shelf holds $5$ different maths books and $3$ different science books. In how many ways can they be arranged if the $3$ science books must be the first three books on the left?

A password has $3$ letters, each one of $A, B, C, D$, and letters may be repeated. There are $64$ passwords in all, and $24$ of them use $3$ different letters. How many passwords have a repeated letter, and what equation connects the three numbers $64$, $24$ and your answer?
A club has $6$ boys and $4$ girls. In how many ways can a captain and a vice-captain (two different people) be chosen if they must be of different gender?

A club has $4$ girls and $6$ boys. There are $90$ ways to choose a president and a vice-president (two different people). In $36$ of these ways the president is a girl. How many ways have a boy as president, and what equation connects $90$, $36$ and your answer?
How many pairs of different whole numbers $a<b$ from $1$ to $20$ have the property that $ab<30$?
